course_name_original: Sistemas de Potencia en Vehículos Híbridos (HEV) y Eléctricos (EV)
course_name_en: Power Systems in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEV) and Electric Vehicles (EV)
prerequisites: Electric Machines for generation and traction
Dynamic analysis and modeling of electrical machines

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Critical analysis of the information coming from sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Asses the risks of the use of electrical energy, as well as those of industrial installations, understanding the necessity of safety elements, protections and signalling in power systems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding the fundamental characteristics, as well as advantages and drawbacks of electrical and hybrid traction systems compared to combustion engines
Acquire the knowledge of power electronics needed to analyse and design electrical and hybrid traction systems

Ability to understand the importance and particular issues of the control and monitoring systems used in electrical and hybrid traction systems (for the Scientific – Technological Research Strand only)

Ability to understand how the different auxiliary systems and sub-systems (lighting and signalling, navigation, communications, etc.) are integrated into the EV/HEV, and how do they constrain the design of the whole system (for the Scientific – Technological Research Strand only)
Ability to understand the necessity for systems and strategies of energy storage and recovery in electrical and hybrid vehicles (for the Scientific – Technological Research Strand only)
Ability of understanding the concepts, strategies and power transmission systems involved in the design of the electrical and hybrid vehicle (for the Scientific – Technological Research Strand only)
Knowing power topologies for EV / HEV.
Selection of traction machines commonly used in electric traction and analyze the implications for the design of the whole system.
To understand the control strategies of power systems of the EV / HEV.
To analyze the different architectures and hybrid electric vehicles, with special emphasis on implications for the power system.
To know auxiliary systems and their relation to vehicle power systems.

syllabus_topics: Overview of electric machine drive requirements for HEV and EV applications
Types of electric machines and which ones best match HEV and EV applications requirements
Power electronics for HEV and EV's, including component choices
Control requirements and algorithms for HEV and EV's
Basics: why HEV/EV/PHEV, constituents of a HEV/EV/PHEV
Series hybrid & Parallel hybrid (pre-transmission/post-transmission/through the road)
HEV: planetary gears, powertrain concepts, continuous variable transmission, modes of operation
PHEV: Architectures, power management, vehicle to grid technology
Electronic Control Units (ECUs) Distribution Electronic Control Units (ECUs) Distribution
assessment_rules: A minimum mark of 4 out of 10 is required for the Final written exam (EX), Project report (PR), and Project presentation (OP). If all minimum requirements are met, the final grade is calculated as: Final grade=0.40⋅EX+0.25⋅PR+0.15⋅OP+0.10⋅HW+0.10⋅PA. If the minimum mark is not achieved in any of these mandatory elements, the final grade will be the minimum between 4.0 and the result of the formula. The extraordinary assessment consists of the same elements and grading calculation as the ordinary assessment.
